  • sum(): Calculates the total sum of values in each group.
  • size(): Returns the number of rows in each group, including those with missing values.
  • count(): Calculates the number of non-missing values in each group.
  • std(): Computes the standard deviation for each group.
  • var(): Calculates the variance for each group.
  • sem(): Computes the standard error of the mean for each group.
  • describe(): Generates a variety of descriptive statistics for each group.
  • first(): Retrieves the first value in each group.
  • last(): Retrieves the last value in each group.
  • nth(n): Takes the nth value from each group.
  • min(): Finds the minimum value within each group.
  • max(): Finds the maximum value within each group.

item.description:

Here are several proven approaches to adjust Pandas display settings for showing all data:

1. Context-Specific Option Management with option_context

A clean method involves temporarily setting display limits within a with block. This ensures that settings revert automatically once the block is exited, avoiding global configuration persistence.

import pandas as pd

# Assume 'df' is your large DataFrame
# Set display limits to show everything within this scope
with pd.option_context('display.max_rows', None, 'display.max_columns', None, 'display.max_colwidth', None):
    print(df)
    # Additional options like 'display.width' can be added here too

If operating within a Jupyter environment, utilizing display(df) instead of print(df) leverages the rich display capabilities inherent to notebooks.

The DataFrame.apply and Series.apply methods in pandas are convenient functions that allow you to apply a user-defined function across rows or columns. Python’s built-in and, or, and not operators attempt to evaluate their operands to a single boolean value. When applied to Pandas Series or NumPy arrays with more than one element, it’s impossible for Python to determine a singular truth value. Should a Series with multiple True and False values be considered True if any element is True, or only if all elements are True? NumPy and Pandas, to avoid making an arbitrary assumption that might lead to incorrect results, raise this ValueError.
